"""align.py — token-level minimum-edit alignment shared by every STT bake-off scorer.

One primitive, used by the WER scorer (CS-8.STT1, P-STT-1 §1.4) and the keyword
scorer (CS-8.LEX1, Contextual Earnings-22 definition), so the two never disagree
about which hypothesis token sits at which reference position.

Contract (P-STT-1 §1.4): a token is a whitespace-delimited unit of the normalised
string; the utterance error count is the Levenshtein distance with unit cost for
substitution, deletion and insertion (S + D + I, no weighting). No fuzzy or
edit-distance-tolerant token matching: two tokens match iff they are equal strings.

The backtrace is deterministic: on equal cost it prefers match/substitution, then
deletion, then insertion, so the same pair of sequences always yields the same
alignment (the determinism property of §1.3 carried over to the reduction).

Pure function module: no I/O, no process, no inference.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import List, Optional, Sequence, Tuple

MATCH = "match"
SUB = "sub"
DEL = "del"  # reference token with no hypothesis token
INS = "ins"  # hypothesis token with no reference token


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class AlignedPair:
    """One alignment column. `ref_idx`/`hyp_idx` are None for INS/DEL respectively."""
    op: str
    ref_idx: Optional[int]
    hyp_idx: Optional[int]
    ref_tok: Optional[str]
    hyp_tok: Optional[str]


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Alignment:
    pairs: Tuple[AlignedPair, ...]
    substitutions: int
    deletions: int
    insertions: int
    n_ref: int
    n_hyp: int

    @property
    def errors(self) -> int:
        return self.substitutions + self.deletions + self.insertions


def edit_distance(ref: Sequence[str], hyp: Sequence[str]) -> int:
    """Levenshtein distance over tokens (unit costs). O(len(ref)*len(hyp)) time, O(len(hyp)) space."""
    ref = list(ref)
    hyp = list(hyp)
    prev = list(range(len(hyp) + 1))
    for i in range(1, len(ref) + 1):
        cur = [i] + [0] * len(hyp)
        r = ref[i - 1]
        for j in range(1, len(hyp) + 1):
            cost = 0 if r == hyp[j - 1] else 1
            cur[j] = min(prev[j - 1] + cost, prev[j] + 1, cur[j - 1] + 1)
        prev = cur
    return prev[-1]


def align(ref: Sequence[str], hyp: Sequence[str]) -> Alignment:
    """Minimum-edit alignment with a deterministic backtrace.

    Primary objective: minimum S+D+I (the P-STT-1 error count). Secondary objective,
    among equal-cost alignments: maximum number of exact matches, so a correctly
    recognised token is aligned to its reference position whenever an optimal
    alignment allows it (the keyword scorer counts a true positive only at the
    aligned position). Remaining ties: match/sub, then deletion, then insertion.
    """
    ref = list(ref)
    hyp = list(hyp)
    n, m = len(ref), len(hyp)
    # cell = (errors, -matches); compared lexicographically.
    d: List[List[Tuple[int, int]]] = [[(0, 0)] * (m + 1) for _ in range(n + 1)]
    for i in range(n + 1):
        d[i][0] = (i, 0)
    for j in range(m + 1):
        d[0][j] = (j, 0)
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        r = ref[i - 1]
        row, up = d[i], d[i - 1]
        for j in range(1, m + 1):
            if r == hyp[j - 1]:
                diag = (up[j - 1][0], up[j - 1][1] - 1)
            else:
                diag = (up[j - 1][0] + 1, up[j - 1][1])
            dele = (up[j][0] + 1, up[j][1])
            inse = (row[j - 1][0] + 1, row[j - 1][1])
            row[j] = min(diag, dele, inse)

    pairs: List[AlignedPair] = []
    s = de = ins = 0
    i, j = n, m
    while i > 0 or j > 0:
        if i > 0 and j > 0:
            eq = ref[i - 1] == hyp[j - 1]
            prev = d[i - 1][j - 1]
            diag = (prev[0], prev[1] - 1) if eq else (prev[0] + 1, prev[1])
            if d[i][j] == diag:
                if not eq:
                    s += 1
                pairs.append(AlignedPair(MATCH if eq else SUB, i - 1, j - 1, ref[i - 1], hyp[j - 1]))
                i -= 1
                j -= 1
                continue
        if i > 0 and d[i][j] == (d[i - 1][j][0] + 1, d[i - 1][j][1]):
            de += 1
            pairs.append(AlignedPair(DEL, i - 1, None, ref[i - 1], None))
            i -= 1
            continue
        ins += 1
        pairs.append(AlignedPair(INS, None, j - 1, None, hyp[j - 1]))
        j -= 1
    pairs.reverse()
    out = Alignment(tuple(pairs), s, de, ins, n, m)
    assert out.errors == d[n][m][0] == edit_distance(ref, hyp)
    return out

"""stt_norm.py — the pinned STT output normalisers (CS-8.STT1 (a)/(b), DP-B).

Three named, versioned, content-hashed normalisers, all pure functions of
``(text, lang, side)``:

``stt_norm/v1`` — Annex S P-STT-1 §1.3 exactly, in the normative order
    (``whisper_stt.NORMALIZATION_STEPS``):

    1. Unicode NFKC, then ``casefold()`` (never ``lower()``).
    2. Non-lexical marker removal from the CLOSED list ``whisper_stt.NONLEXICAL_MARKERS``
       (compared in NFKC+casefold form), counted per utterance. A marker-shaped span
       NOT on the list (``[applause]``, ``(inaudible)``) is NOT removed: it is reported
       in ``unknown_markers`` and the utterance routes to the ``unknown_marker`` class.
       ``<unk>`` is exempt from marker shape: it is the Parakeet-family unknown token,
       counted in ``unk_count`` and scored as an ordinary (wrong) token, never excluded.
    3. Every character outside ``[\\w\\s']`` becomes a SPACE (never deleted).
    4. Apostrophes kept (``don't`` stays one token).
    5. Hyphen split (already done by step 3; declared so the choice is visible).
    6. Numerals, HYPOTHESIS side only, through a CLOSED enumerated table into the
       reference's spelled form. A digit-bearing token not in the table, or a complex
       numeral span (``3.5``, ``1,920``, ``$5``, ``5%``), is ``numeral_uncovered`` —
       COULD_NOT_CHECK, never guessed. On the REFERENCE side digits are never converted
       (the reference is the fixed side); a digit-bearing reference token is flagged
       ``numeral_uncovered`` too, because the hyp->ref direction cannot be checked
       against a reference that is not in spelled form.
    7. Whitespace collapse and strip — always last.

    v1 has NO filler step: fillers are ordinary words.

``stt_norm/v2`` — CANDIDATE (never pooled or differenced with v1 until CS-2 ratifies):
    v1 plus (i) typographic apostrophes ``’`` (U+2019) and ``ʼ`` (U+02BC) folded to
    ``'`` immediately after casefold — NFKC does not fold them, so under v1 ``l’uomo``
    is two tokens while ``l'uomo`` is one; (ii) fr/it elision rule: an elided form

    splitting; (iii) closed it/de/fr numeral tables beside the English one.
    German compounds are NOT merged or split by the normaliser; the scorer counts
    them as their own error class (``de_compound_split_join``) and forgives nothing.
    DP-B: fillers (``uh``, ``um``, ``euh``, ``ähm`` …) are ordinary words — never deleted
    from either side. ``FILLERS`` exists ONLY to flag ``fillers_in_ref``.

a normaliser that can read the reference can rewrite the hypothesis toward it, which

"""Prompt bytes for OCC-1. The QUESTION block and answer rules are byte-identical across arms;
only the carrier (text reference vs rendered frames) and its one-paragraph description differ.

Wording adapted from @oh-my-pi/snapcompact research/prompts/{qa-text,qa-image-multi}.md (MIT).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import base64
import hashlib
import json

RULES = (
    "- Give short extractive answers: a word or phrase copied from the text.\n"
    "- If you cannot find or cannot read the information, reply exactly UNREADABLE for that question.\n"
    "- Output a numbered list, one answer per line, no commentary."
)

TEXT_HEAD = "Below is reference material. Questions follow in the next block.\n\n<reference>\n"
TEXT_TAIL = "\n</reference>\n\nAnswer the questions using ONLY the reference material above.\n" + RULES

IMAGE_HEAD = (
    "The attached {k} image(s) contain encyclopedia passages rendered as dense bitmaps: monospace "
    "pixel font, {cols} characters per row, up to {rows} rows per image. The text flows "
    "continuously across the images: read each image left-to-right, top-to-bottom, then continue "
    "with the next image in order (image 1 first, image {k} last). Original paragraph breaks were "
    "collapsed to spaces."
)
IMAGE_TAIL = "Answer the questions using ONLY text you can read in the images.\n" + RULES


def question_block(questions: list[dict]) -> str:
    return "Questions:\n" + "\n".join(f"{i + 1}. {q['q']}" for i, q in enumerate(questions))


def text_messages(context: str, questions: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:
    content = [
        {"type": "text", "text": TEXT_HEAD + context + TEXT_TAIL},
        {"type": "text", "text": question_block(questions)},
    ]
    return [{"role": "user", "content": content}]


def image_messages(pngs: list[bytes], cols: int, rows: int, questions: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:
    content: list[dict] = [{"type": "text", "text": IMAGE_HEAD.format(k=len(pngs), cols=cols, rows=rows)}]
    for png in pngs:
        url = "data:image/png;base64," + base64.b64encode(png).decode("ascii")
        content.append({"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": url}})
    content.append({"type": "text", "text": IMAGE_TAIL})
    content.append({"type": "text", "text": question_block(questions)})
    return [{"role": "user", "content": content}]


def fingerprint(obj) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(obj, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")).encode()).hexdigest()

Du subsequently based himself in Sichuan for most of the next five years . By the autumn of that year he was in financial trouble , and sent poems begging help to various acquaintances . He was relieved by Yan Wu , a friend and former colleague who was appointed governor general at Chengdu . Despite his financial problems , this was one of the happiest and most peaceful periods of his life . Many of Du 's poems from this period are peaceful depictions of his life at " thatched hut " . In 762 , he left the city to escape a rebellion , but he returned in summer 764 when he was appointed an advisor to Yan , who was involved in campaigns against the Tibetan Empire .
